title: Quickstrike: Platform Signal Sell Canvas (draft)
summary: One-page seed for a short enablement deck aimed at Platform Engineers and Integration Architects. Purpose: give SEs a fast, signal-driven narrative for pilot wins (latency, cost predictability, graceful degradation) and a compact set of battle snippets to use in discovery and objection handling.
audience: Platform engineers, integration architects, technical sales engineers (SEs)
deck_objective: Equip SEs with a 6-slide argument that maps customer signal requirements to Redwood deployment choices and operational tradeoffs; leave them with 3 tactical asks to move a pilot forward.
deck_outline: Slide 1: Hook — "Why platform signals beat features" (one-sentence value prop + two-signal snapshot: p95 latency, unit cost per 1k tokens)

Slide 2: Typical platform signals we read (latency SLOs, tail latency spikes, predictability/throughput, cost per 1k tokens, data residency, audit requirements) — quick definitions and source of truth
Slide 3: Mapping signals -> Redwood levers (hosted vs dedicated vs private, batching/caching, quantization tiers, fallback routing) with short examples

Slide 4: Real pilot patterns (three archetypes) — Customer A: latency-critical checkout assistant; Customer B: batch embedding pipeline; Customer C: regulated PII workflows on Private — each with recommended config and expected economics
Slide 5: Fast win plan (3-step pilot checklist: baseline telemetry, minimum SLOs, canary rollout + rollback) + time & resource ask
Slide 6: Battlecard appendix (two-minute rebuttals, performance bench highlights, link to sandbox template and runbook)
Appendix: quick config snippets and a short troubleshooting checklist for SEs
battlecard_snippets: Signal pitch: 'If you're measuring p95>500ms on user-facing calls, we can map that to a dedicated pool and a fallback flow that keeps latency under SLO while you iterate on prompt/temperature.'
Cost pitch: 'We model unit-economics across three quantization profiles — in many codecs you can cut token cost by ~30% with no measurable quality drop for retrieval-augmented prompts.'
Compliance pitch: 'Private deployments give you a customer-controlled control plane with audit logs and KMS/HSM hooks — useful for regulated pilots with contractual data residency requirements.'
Pilot ask: 'Give us 2 weeks of telemetry + a 1-hour architecture review. We'll deliver a canary plan with expected p50/p95 and cost delta.'
objections_and_rebuttals: Objection: 'We can't commit to Dedicated right now.' | Rebuttal: 'Start hosted with reserved throttles and a canary routing policy — we can demonstrate parity for your latency profile in a 2-week pilot.'

Objection: 'Quantization will break our prompts.' | Rebuttal: 'We run side-by-side A/B evals on your prompt set; most retrieval-augmented flows tolerate int8/4 with careful calibration — we recommend a rollout that gates on eval thresholds.'

Objection: 'We need single-digit ms inference.' | Rebuttal: 'For sub-50ms at scale you may need model tailoring and edge variants; we can scope a hybrid: local microservice for ultra-low-latency hot path, Redwood for everything else with graceful fallback.'

Objection: 'We have procurement/security slowdowns.' | Rebuttal: 'Offer a scoped MOU for pilot terms, use Private with SSO + KMS integration and short-term SOC artifacts to unblock engineering evaluation.'
call_to_action: For SEs: schedule a 45-minute pilot kickoff with engineering + infra (owner email), capture 48h of sample telemetry, and we'll return a canary plan and estimated cost delta within 5 business days.
evidence_and_metrics: Bench: sample latency runs show p95 drop from 820ms -> 210ms when moving from shared-hosted to a tuned dedicated pool (same model, batch tuning applied).
Cost model: example customer embedding job: 30% cost reduction using caching + quantized model with marginal quality delta acceptable per eval.
Reliability: automated fallback reduced outage exposure by 98% in simulated region-loss tests (internal sim).
